summary: Defines the formal Uniform Resource Name namespace for the International Standard Audiovisual Number (ISAN), a numbering system that gives audiovisual works unique international identifiers. The document registers the namespace so ISANs can be used as URNs. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: Every movie can get its own serial number, like a barcode. This memo says how to write that number so computers can use it like a web name.

questions: what is an international standard audiovisual number
how do you express an isan as a urn
subtitle: Unique worldwide identifiers for films and television shows.

tldr.problem: Audiovisual works like movies and TV shows need a worldwide numbering system to identify them uniquely, and this needs to work with internet technology.
tldr.mechanism: ISAN (International Standard Audiovisual Number) is an externally managed numbering system that RFC 4246 registers as a URN namespace, so ISANs can be expressed as standard internet resource names.
tldr.outcome: The ISAN system can now be used in internet-based applications like streaming media services, archives and rights management systems.

today: RFC 4246 remains the definition of the ISAN URN namespace. It is an Informational RFC and has not been obsoleted, so ISAN URNs are registered and usable.

sections.title: What is ISAN?
sections.content:
ISAN stands for International Standard Audiovisual Number. It is a standard system for assigning unique worldwide identifiers to audiovisual works—anything with moving pictures, including films, television shows, and related materials like subtitling tracks.

RFC 4246 is not about ISAN itself, which is defined externally by the ISO and managed by the ISAN International Agency. Instead, this RFC defines how to express ISAN numbers as URNs (Uniform Resource Names), which are internet-standard ways to write resource identifiers.
sections.plainLanguage: ISAN is like a barcode for movies. This document explains how to write that barcode as a computer address, so the internet can use it.

sections.title: URN Namespace Structure
sections.content:
An ISAN expressed as a URN follows the pattern URN:ISAN:[ISAN-NSS], where [ISAN-NSS] is the actual ISAN number. The RFC provides two example forms:

  • URN:ISAN:0123-1230-3210-2310-1 (without version extension)
  • URN:ISAN:1881-66C7-3420-6541-9-9F3A-0245-U (with version extension)

The ISAN number is unique and never reused. The ISAN International Agency, located in Geneva and established through ISO processes, guarantees uniqueness and maintains persistence of the identifiers.
sections.plainLanguage: An ISAN as a web name looks like URN:ISAN: followed by the number. That number is unique forever and never gets given to a different movie.

sections.title: Syntax and Format
sections.content:
The ISAN-NSS is made up of hexadecimal characters (0-9, A-F) arranged in groups separated by hyphens. The structure has three main parts:

  • A root: three groups of four hexadecimal digits each (12 digits total)
  • An episode: one group of four digits plus a check digit
  • Optionally a version: additional groups for version extensions plus another check digit

The check digits use a validation scheme to detect syntax errors. The ISAN-NSS is case-insensitive; uppercase and lowercase characters are treated as identical.
sections.plainLanguage: The number is written in computer-style hexadecimal (0-9, A-F) with groups split by hyphens. The last digit or two in each group is a checksum that catches typing mistakes.

sections.title: Registration and Resolution
sections.content:
Any approved entity can request an ISAN number from the ISAN International Agency by providing required metadata and paying a registration fee. The Agency may delegate this work to regional or market-based registration agencies.

ISAN numbers are resolved through direct or indirect lookup with the ISAN International Agency. At the time of writing, a non-commercial manual system was available online. Resolution procedures may be modified by the Agency as needed.
sections.plainLanguage: Movie studios and archives can ask the ISAN Agency to give them a number for their work. Then they can look up that number later to find information about the film.

sections.title: Use Cases and Scope
sections.content:
ISAN is used primarily by producers and studios of audiovisual works, but also by film and video archives, libraries, rights administrators, program guide services, and audience measurement services. The system is not limited to major works; any bona fide entity can register any work, though the greatest value comes from widely distributed works.

The potential for use in the internet community is as an identifier for streaming media services, content management systems, and digital rights applications. The scope of ISAN URNs is global.
sections.plainLanguage: Movie studios use ISAN to track their films, but so do libraries, streaming services and companies that track who watches what. Anyone can register a film, but big blockbusters get the most use out of it.

references.text: Daigle, L., van Gulik, D., Iannella, R., and P. Faltstrom, "Uniform Resource Names (URN) Namespace Definition Mechanisms", BCP 66, RFC 3406, October 2002.
